newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada buys Canadian dollars - traders.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada buys Canadian dollars - traders.

text.p: The Bank of Canada intervened on Thursday and bought Canadian dollars for U.S. dollars as the currency traded around the C$1.3450 level, dealers said.
The intervention was through brokers and considered light after the currency weakened more than 50 basis points from this morning's C$1.3388.

Analysts said the central bank might also be doing business on behalf of the government of Canada, which had a semi-annual coupon payment of US$48 million due today for a C$1.5 billion global bond due on July 21, 2005 and issued on July 21, 1995 with a coupon of 6.375 percent.
After the intervention, the Canadian dollar was trading at C$1.3446 after opening at C$1.3388 and Wednesday's close of C$1.3375. Traders expected further losses.
The Bank of Canada does not comment on intervention.
